name: Software developers

why: System-level design and trade-off decisions still need a human

claims.text: PwC's 2026 Barometer lists software developers among the roles AI democratises: it automates higher-expertise tasks and leaves the role requiring less expertise, with lower barriers to entry and falling wages.

In Canada, the monthly hiring rate for 15–29-year-olds in coding-intensive occupations fell from 2.5% to 1.9% between the six months to November 2022 and the six months to August 2026, while their separation rate rose from 2.4% to 3.5%, a series the authors call volatile on a small sample.

The same study finds hiring rates fell furthest where AI exposure is lowest (4.0% to 3.3%), that coding hiring started falling in early 2022, and that separation rates were flat across exposure groups — so it does not attribute the coding decline to AI.
In the first quarter of 2026, 4.5% of US software development postings were entry-level and 69.3% were senior, against 46% entry-level and about 14% senior across the whole US labour market.
